anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of On Pascha exists (Toura 1941; Daly ACW 54 and Witte's German are copyrighted and were not copied). Sense checked against the locked Witte Greek (and, for 1.94, Victor of Capua's Latin as Witte prints it) and the wording of the cited scriptures.

apparatus: Mostly unrestored or heavily restored Greek; English does not fill gaps.

bible_refs.note: They are continent for a perishable crown; we for an imperishable.
Leave none of the meats until morning.

pass_a_gloss: For if someone is athletic [gap] competing and looking to those being continent for the sake of a perishable contest, so that they may receive a perishable contest, but he himself pursuing to receive an imperishable. For if someone should so gird the loin, he will also be able to leave nothing of the meats until morning.
pass_b_english: For if someone is athletic [...] competing and looking to those who are continent for the sake of a perishable contest, that they may receive a perishable contest, while he himself pursues an imperishable one to receive. For if someone should so gird the loin, he will also be able to leave none of the meats until morning (1 Corinthians 9:25) (Exodus 12:10).
source_text: Εἴ τις γὰρ ἀθλητικὸς ... τ ... λογον ε ... νως με..α ... δυ...αι των..ε ... εται..ν ... ις ἀγῶ[ν]ιζ[όμε]νος καὶ ἀφορῶν εἰς [τοὺς ἕ]νεκεν φθαρτοῦ ἀγῶ[νος ἐγ]κρατευομένους, ἵνα [φθαρ]τὸν ἀγῶνα λάβωσιν, [α]ὐτ[ὸς] δὲ ἄφθαρτον διώκων [λα]βεῖν. Εἰ γὰρ οὕτως περιζώσαιτό τις τὴν ὀσφύν, δυνήσεται καὶ μηδὲν τῶν κρεῶν καταλιπεῖν ἕως πρωΐ.
